newsitem.title: USA: "Breakdown" takes top spot at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Breakdown" takes top spot at U.S. box office.

text.p: The Kurt Russell thriller "Breakdown" and the Mike Myers spy spoof "Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery" were the two most popular films at the box office over the weekend, estimates said Sunday.

"Breakdown," in which Russell searches for his kidnapped wife, took in about $12.7 million in ticket sales for the Friday to Sunday period, according to studio estimates compiled by Exhibitor Relations Co. Inc.
Its average of $6,025 from 2,108 screens augurs well for the picture, which is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..

Fellow newcomer "Austin Powers," which pokes fun at James Bond movies and the "Swinging London" of the 1960s, grabbed second with $10.0 million. The New Line Cinema release averaged a more modest $4,572 from 2,187 screens.

Al Shapiro, the studio's head of domestic theatrical distribution, said the movie did slightly better than expected. He credited a "fun marketing campaign" and heavy promotion by star/writer Myers for its performance.
New Line is a unit of Time Warner Inc..

Last weekend's number one, "Volcano," fell to third with $9.5 million. The film fell 35 percent from last weekend, and averaged $3,422 from 2,776 screens. It is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp..

Jim Carrey's "Liar Liar" was steady in fourth with $5.8 million. The comedy has earned $151.5 million after 45 days in release. It slipped just 19 percent from last weekend, and averaged $2,165 from 2,679 screens. Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd., released the picture.

"Romy and Michele's High School Reunion" fell three places to fifth in its second weekend with $5.6 million. The 10-day total for the Lisa Kudrow-Mira Sorvino comedy is $15.1 million. This weekend, the Walt Disney Co. picture slipped 25 percent and averaged $3,487 from 1,606 screens.

The only other new entrant in the top 10 was the MGM fantasy adventure "Warriors of Virtue," which opened in seventh with $3.6 million in sales at the box office. It averaged $1,713 from 2,101 screens. MGM is owned by Kirk Kerkorian and Australia's Seven Network Ltd.
